resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive dates the front range to 1853 and records it as lost; LF describes the 1853 framework, a third front-range structure of 1867, and the fire of 1910 that destroyed the front-range light. Both the 1853 date and the 1867 replacement are supported; the building lost in 1910 is the 1867 structure.

The archive gives the original optic type as reflectors and a lens installed in 1862. LF says the lantern room and lens from the 1839 tower were moved to the 1862 tower. The archive's type and LF's account are both recorded; the lens type is not stated in the sources used here.

LF says the tower and lantern were removed after deactivation and the restored lighthouse was made the centrepiece of the 2001 resort. Rowlett says the light tower was replaced in a 2000-01 restoration. The two accounts differ and are both recorded; the present height is not confirmed.

notes_for_editor: The Light-House Board volumes for 1837-1890 are not in the local corpus, so the 1837-1838 appropriations and the 1839 construction rest on LighthouseFriends (LF). The 1891 and 1894 Board pages (scan 191, 504) and the 1922 Commissioner page (scan 756, printed 56) were checked against the corpus page index. The Platt quotation is LF's quotation of an 1838 report and has not been read in the original. The USLHS keeper roster ends in 1904 with Daniel Finn; LF's later keepers Frank Ritter (to 1929) and Henry Waibel (to 1948) belong to the Sandusky Bay inner and outer range records, which are separate and not used here. The 1910 Eastland fire is LF's account, with Rowlett's year; no newspaper check was made (the Chronicling America search was not run for this station). The two NRHP nominations (82001449, 84003667) are not digitised; only the NPGallery asset pages were read. Their 'Date Published' fields are 20 October 1982 for 82001449, a record titled 'U.S. Coast Guard Building' in the Sandusky MRA and not the lighthouse, and 19 July 1984 for 84003667, 'Cedar Point Light'. Bulletin 'Cedar Point' hits in the 1912-1939 Bulletin volumes are Cedar Point, Maryland, and were excluded. The record gives the rear range 12.2 m 'standing'; LF says the tower was removed after 1904 and Rowlett says a tower was replaced in 2000-01, so the record's height may refer to the 1862 tower. The archive's focal height and the 1862 lens date are as the archive gives them. Lighthouse Point's counts (156 cottages and cabins, 145 RV sites) come from the Six Flags page and may change.
